xcode.device-support.name: Device support files
xcode.device-support.what: Debug information Xcode copies from an iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Apple TV or Vision Pro the first time you connect it, one folder per system version.
xcode.device-support.if-removed: The folder goes to the Trash. You can still build and run apps; debugging on a device of that version waits until Xcode copies the files again.
xcode.device-support.comes-back: Yes, when you connect a device on that version again. Copying takes a few minutes.
xcode.previews.name: Xcode previews
xcode.previews.what: What Xcode builds to show your SwiftUI previews.
xcode.previews.if-removed: What is inside the folder goes to the Trash and the folder stays.
xcode.previews.comes-back: Yes, the next time you open a preview. The first one takes longer.
xcode.simulator-caches.name: Simulator caches
xcode.simulator-caches.what: Files the iOS simulators keep to start faster, one set for each version of macOS you ran them on.
xcode.simulator-caches.if-removed: What is inside the folder goes to the Trash and the folder stays. Your simulators and their apps stay.
xcode.simulator-caches.comes-back: Yes, the next time a simulator starts. That start takes longer.
xcode.archives.name: Xcode archives
xcode.archives.what: The builds you archived in Xcode to publish an app, each with the debug symbols of that version.
xcode.archives.made-by: Xcode, when you choose Product, then Archive.
xcode.archives.if-removed: The archive goes to the Trash. Without it you cannot read the crash reports of that version or publish that build again.
xcode.archives.comes-back: No. Keep the archives of every version people still use.
xcode.enabled.label: Xcode's files
xcode.enabled.description: Finds device support files, previews, simulator caches and archives that Xcode keeps, while Xcode and the Simulator are closed. They go to the Trash.
xcode.reason.device-support: Debug files for {platform} {version} take {size}. Xcode copies them again if you connect a device on this version.
xcode.reason.device-support-recent: Debug files for {platform} {version} take {size}. This is one of the newest versions here, so a device you use may need them; Xcode copies them again when you connect it.
xcode.reason.previews: Xcode's previews take {size}. Xcode builds them again when you open a preview.
xcode.reason.simulator-caches: The simulators' caches take {size}. They are made again the next time a simulator starts.
xcode.reason.archive: Archived on {date}, {size}. It holds the debug symbols of that build: keep it if that version is still in use.
xcode.left-out.special: It holds a connection a running program may be using, so it is kept.
xcode.left-out.not-yours: Some of it belongs to the system or another user, or is locked, often after a command run with sudo. Removing it needs an administrator.
xcode.left-out.no-system: Fresher could not list your open apps, so it keeps this. Scan again.
xcode.left-out.app-open: Xcode or the Simulator is open and may be using this. Quit them and scan again.
